First Earl of Westmorland. His marriage to Juana Beaufort linked the Nevilles to the descendants of Juan de Ghent. Among his sons were Ricardo de Salisbury and Cecilia, mother of Edward IV and Richard III.

A daughter of John of Gaunt and Katherine Swynford. Through her marriage to Ralph Neville she was the mother of Cecily Neville and Richard, Earl of Salisbury; her descendants connected the principal Yorkist leaders.
Earl of Salisbury through his marriage to Alice Montagu and father of Warwick. He supported Richard of York and was executed after the defeat at Wakefield in 1460.
Countess of Salisbury and wife of Richard Neville. Her inheritance strengthened this branch of the Nevilles, and she was the mother of the Earl of Warwick.
Earl of Warwick, known as the Kingmaker. He helped Edward IV gain the throne, subsequently broke with him and took part in Henry VI’s restoration. He died fighting at Barnet in 1471.

Warwick's heir and Ricardo Neville's wife. Her daughters Elizabeth and Anne married George of Clarence and Ricardo of Gloucester, respectively, linking Warwick's inheritance with her brothers and sisters.
The elder daughter of Warwick and Anne Beauchamp married George of Clarence in 1469. She was the mother of Edward, Earl of Warwick, whose identity Lambert Simnel’s promoters used in 1487.
Duke of Clarence and brother of Edward IV and Ricardo III. He allied with Warwick with Edward, reconciled with his king in 1471 and became convicted of treason and executed in 1478.
The only son of Henry VI and Margaret of Anjou. His right to come about was moved by his 1460 agreement with Ricardo of York. He married Ana Neville and died at Tewkesbury in 1471.

Brother of Edmundo Tudor and uncle of Henry VII. He held up the Lancatrian cause and protected his nephew during his exile and participated in his expedition of 1485. Henry VII created him Duke of Bedford.
Duke of York and son of Edward IV and Isabel Woodville. He was housed at the Tower of London with his brother Edward V in 1483. The date and circumstances of his death are unknown.
The son of Richard III and Anne Neville received his title as Prince of Wales after his father's coronation. His death in 1484 left Richard III without a legitimate surviving child.

Count of Warwick and son of Jorge de Clarence and Isabel Neville. Henry VII held him prisoner at the Tower. In 1487 Lambert Simnel's proponents put his boy through this Yorkist heir. He was executed in 1499.

Duke of Somerset and a leading supporter of Henry VI. His rivalry with Richard of York over government and royal patronage contributed to the political crisis. He died at the first Battle of St Albans in 1455.

eventos.descripcion: The extinction of the direct Capetian line opens up a dispute after his death: Felipe de Valois is crowned as Philip VI while Edward III retains a dynastic claim by his mother Elizabeth of France.
The english victory of Créby confirms the efficacy of his combined armies and gives Edward III a dominant position in the first phase of the war.
The Black Prince's army defeats John II of France and captures the king, leading the French monarchy to a political and financial crisis.
The agreement recognizes an enormous expansion of the British domains in France in exchange for important dines.
Charles V and Bertrand du Guesclin avoid great battle and get back a great share of the territories lost by France.
The Frankopan artillery defeats John Talbot's army at Castillon. The loss of Guyena conventionally closed the One hundred Age War.
Charles V gradually distributes his domains between the Spanish branch and the Austrian branch of the Habsburgés.
Philip II's naval expedition against England fails after fighting, logistical problems and adverse time.
After the collapse of the Hohenstaufen authority, several rival kings are fighting an imperial crown whose ability to impose obedience is deeply weakened.

eventos.titulo: Henry VIII breaks up with Rome
eventos.descripcion: The real supremacy about the Church of England turns a matrimonial and political crisis into an ecclesiastical rupture of lasting consequences.
Following the confessional tours of Henry VIII, Edward VI and Mary I, Elizabeth I comforts a Church of England separate from Rome with his own Protestant identity.
The death of Francis of Anjou makes Henry of Navarra an alleged heir. Enrique de Guisa reorganizes the Catholic League, backed from Spain, to prevent a Protestant from inheriting the French crown.

eventos.titulo: Pius V gets the Holy League
eventos.descripcion: Pius V has an agreement between the Hispanic Monarchy, Venice and the Pontifical States. Philip II provides an essential part of the resources and his stepbrother Don Juan of Austria receives the supreme command of the Allied fleet.
The forces of William Wallace and Andrew Moray defeat an english army at Stirling Bridge, one of the great challenges of the first Scottish war of independence.

eventos.titulo: Robert Bruce is crowned King of Scotland
eventos.descripcion: Following John Comyn's death, Robert Bruce claims his crown and is crowned at Scone as Roberto I.
The great victory of Roberto I with his army strengthens the political and military recovery of the Scottish monarchy.

name: Navarre
summary: Navarre’s position in the Pyrenees connected its history with French houses and the Iberian kingdoms. In 1234 Theobald of Champagne succeeded his uncle Sancho VII through rights transmitted by Blanche of Navarre. Joan I’s marriage to Philip IV later united Navarre and France in their descendants, but in 1328 the two crowns followed different successions. Joan II and Philip of Évreux opened a new Navarrese phase. After Blanche I, disputes between John of Aragon and his children ultimately carried the inheritance through Eleanor to the Foix. Catherine and John of Albret faced the conquest of 1512. The later territorial division requires a distinction among the claimed crown, effective rule and the monarchy’s continuity north of the Pyrenees.

King of Aragon and Navarra, central figure of the dynastic conflicts of the Iberian peninsula of the 15th century. He was the father of Fernando the Catholic and key piece in the expansion of the Statámara.

King of Aragon and, together with Elizabeth I, the protagonist of the dynastic union of the Hispanic crowns. Its policy combined the consolidation of the peninsula, the Mediterranean expansion and intense marriage diplomacy.
Queen of Castile and Aragon, daughter of the Catholic Kings and mother of Charles V. He kept his crowns while Felipe, Fernando and Carlos subsequently exercised the government.

people.nombre: Gaston of Foix, Prince of Viana
people.resumen: The son of Gaston IV of Foix and Eleanor of Navarre, he married Magdalene of France and was the father of Francis Phoebus and Catherine. He died before his mother succeeded to the Navarrese throne, so his rights passed to his children.
He inherited Navarra as a minor, under the regency of his mother Magdalena of France. His premature death led to his sister Catherine's succession.
He ruled Navarra with Juan de Albret during the conquest of the peninsular part by Fernando the Catholic. The dynasty retained its rights and domains north of the Pyrenees.

The son of Alain of Albret and Françoise of Châtillon, married Catherine of Navarra. His position was a royal from that marriage, while his home of birth was Albret. The conquest of 1512 displaced the center of his monarchy and left his offspring a divided territorial and political heritage.
He maintained the Albret's claim on the Peninsular Navarre after the conquest. His marriage to Marguerite of Navarre turned his court into a focus of Renaissance culture.

King of Spain during a stage of great cultural glow and strong political crises. His reign, associated with the condeduke of Olivares, was marked by European wars and the rebellions of Catalonia and Portugal.
He actively intervened in the crises of the French monarchy during the Hundred Years’ War. His naval and Norman domains allowed him to act on both sides of the Pyrenees.

King of Navarre during the second half of the twelfth century and the father of Sancho VII and Blanche of Navarre. His family connected the kingdom with Castile and Champagne. Blanche’s descendants were decisive in the succession of 1234, when the crown passed to Theobald I.

King of Navarre, famous for his participation at Las Navas de Tolosa. His long reign closed the direct male line of Navarre’s Jiménez dynasty.

Prince of the House of Bourbon. Their life was connected with France, Navarre.

Prince of the Bourbon dynasty. Their career was connected to France and Navarre.
Last King of France of the Old Regime. The financial crisis and the call for the General States led to the French Revolution, which ended with the monarchy and its implementation.
Last King Habsburg of Spain. His lack of offspring turned his succession into a European question and, after his death, he triggered the Spanish War of Succession.

King of Spain between 1746 and 1759, son of Philip V and Mary Luisa of Savoy. He maintained a policy of neutrality and reforms with ministers such as Ensenada and Carvajal; he died without offspring.

people.resumen: The daughter of Charles II of Navarra, first married John IV of Brittany and was the mother of several members of the next ducal generation. She later married Henry IV of England.

people.nombre: Margaret of Foix, Duchess of Brittany
people.resumen: A daughter of Gaston IV of Foix and Eleanor of Navarre, she married Francis II of Brittany and was the mother of Anne of Brittany. Her position provides a direct link between the Pyrenean houses and the Breton succession.

people.nombre: Agnes of Navarre, Countess of Foix
people.resumen: Daughter of Philip of Évreux and Juana II of Navarre, married Gaston Fébus. She was the mother of the Count's legitimate son, also called Gaston.

people.nombre: John of Foix, Viscount of Narbonne
people.resumen: The son of Gaston IV and Leonor of Navarre, he was the brother of Gaston, Prince of Viana, and uncle of Catherine of Navarre. He married Maria of Orleans. His sons Germana and Gaston of Nemours link this branch with the Aragonese court and with the French campaigns in Italy.

The daughter of Blanche I of Navarre and John of Aragon, and the sister of Charles of Viana and Eleanor. After Charles’s death she stood at the centre of the dispute over Navarrese succession rights against her father.

personas.resumen: King of France who strengthened the administration and authority of the Crown. Their conflict with Boniface VIII and the fall of the Templars symbolize the growing strength of the French monarchy.

A daughter of Theobald I of Navarre and Margaret of Bourbon, she married Hugh IV of Burgundy. Her career extended the connections of the house of Champagne beyond its French and Navarrese inheritance and into other ducal houses.
He inherited Navarre through his mother Blanche, linking the kingdom to the comital House of Champagne. He was also a distinguished poet in the French trouvère tradition.
Consort of the Dampierre dynasty. Their career was connected to Navarre, Champagne.

Daughter of Theobaldo I of Navarre and Inés de Beaujeu, she married John I of Brittany. She was the mother of John II. Her position directly connects the Navarre dynasty of Champagne with the Breton dukes and helps to follow the relations between the two regions developed in this update.

Daughter of Robert I of Artois, Blanca was Queen consort of Navarra for her marriage to Henry I. When she sent in 1274 she defended her daughter Juana's inheritance and negotiated her link with the future Philip IV of France. Her second marriage, with Edmundo de Lancaster, connected the house with the English monarchy.
His short reign left Navarre to his daughter Joan, still a child. The heiress’s minority facilitated the French monarchy’s involvement in the kingdom’s affairs.
He combined the kingship of Navarre with the government of Champagne. He accompanied Louis IX on the Tunis crusade and died on the return journey.
Consort of the Capeto dynasty. Their career was connected to Navarre.
His marriage to Philip IV linked Navarra to the French monarchy without erasing his identity as a kingdom. He also preserved the Comital heritage of Champagne.
His access to the crown after Louis X and the newborn John I consolidated the exclusion of women from the French succession. Navarra would end up following a different dynastic solution.

King of Aragon and Navarra, central figure of the dynastic conflicts of the Iberian peninsula of the 15th century. He was the father of Fernando the Catholic and key piece in the expansion of the Statámara.

King of Aragon and, together with Elizabeth I, the protagonist of the dynastic union of the Hispanic crowns. Its policy combined the consolidation of the peninsula, the Mediterranean expansion and intense marriage diplomacy.
Queen of Castile and Aragon, daughter of the Catholic Kings and mother of Charles V. He kept his crowns while Felipe, Fernando and Carlos subsequently exercised the government.

Emperor of the Holy Empire and sovereign of a composite monarchy that reached the Iberian peninsula, Italy, the Netherlands and America. From Philip I he inherited the County of Burgundy, Artois, Namur and Luxembourg, as well as other Dutch territories. He then incorporated Frisia, Utrecht, Overijssel, Drente, Groninga and Güeldres in a step-by-step manner between 1524 and 1543. He preserved the ducal dignity of Burgundy, but did not rule the duchy incorporated into France. Since 1535, Milan has been under imperial control; Philip II's invasion and subsequent possession must be distinguished from that government.

King of the Hispanic Monarchy at the time of its maximum European and Atlantic projection. During his reign, Lepanto, the dynastic union with Portugal and the great rebellion of the Netherlands took place.
It favored internal stability and the development of the court of the Navarre in Olite. The Union's mandate ended the institutional division of the Burgos of Pamplona.
Consort of the Trastámara dynasty. Their life was connected with Navarre.
He inherited Navarra and ruled it with Juan de Aragón. His death opened the conflict between her husband and his son Charles, Prince of Viana.
His marriage with Leonor de Navarra linked his house to his Navarre succession. He combined his prenaic interests with his service to his French monarchy.
Prince of the House of Trastámara. Their life was connected with Navarre.
He was king of Navarra for his marriage to Juana II. He participated in penisterial campaigns and died after the expedition against Algeciras.
Daughter of Louis of Évreux and Margarita of Artois, married Charles IV of France. Her marriage connected the branch of Evreux with the main line of the capet kings.
His death left open the French succession while waiting for the birth of an heir. John I's brief life and the exclusion of Juana favored the promotion of Philip V.
Consort of the Burgundy dynasty. Their career was connected to France, Navarre.
He was king from birth and died a few days later. His reign illustrates how an extreme minority could turn succession into a question of regency and dynastic legitimacy.
She recovered the Navarrese crown after being excluded from the French succession. Her reign with Philip of Évreux separated the political trajectories of Navarre and France once more.
Consort of the Ivrea-Burgundy dynasty. Their life was connected with France and Navarre.
He was the last French king of the Capet's direct male line. His death without a son opened the succession that led Philip VI of Valois to the throne.
Daughter of Philip of Évreux and Joan II of Navarre, she married Philip VI of France. The marriage brought the Navarrese house into close connection with the first generation of Valois rulers.
Consort of the Valois dynasty. Their career was connected to Navarre and France.
Consort of the Valois-Angoulême dynasty. Their career was connected to France and Navarre.
Consort of the Valois-Angoulême dynasty. Their career was connected to France and Navarre.
Noble of the Valois dynasty. Their career was connected to France, Navarre.
Her succession rights were entangled with the family conflict involving John II and the Prince of Viana. She was queen regnant of Navarre for only a few weeks before her death.

personas.nombre: Gaston of Foix, Prince of Viana
personas.resumen: The son of Gaston IV of Foix and Eleanor of Navarre, he married Magdalene of France and was the father of Francis Phoebus and Catherine. He died before his mother succeeded to the Navarrese throne, so his rights passed to his children.
He inherited Navarra as a minor, under the regency of his mother Magdalena of France. His premature death led to his sister Catherine's succession.
He ruled Navarra with Juan de Albret during the conquest of the peninsular part by Fernando the Catholic. The dynasty retained its rights and domains north of the Pyrenees.

The son of Alain of Albret and Françoise of Châtillon, married Catherine of Navarra. His position was a royal from that marriage, while his home of birth was Albret. The conquest of 1512 displaced the center of his monarchy and left his offspring a divided territorial and political heritage.
He maintained the Albret's claim on the Peninsular Navarre after the conquest. His marriage to Marguerite of Navarre turned his court into a focus of Renaissance culture.
He adopted the Reformation and turned his domains into a fundamental support of the Hugonote cause. He was the mother of Henry of Navarra, future Henry IV of France.
His marriage to Juana de Albret gave him the dignity of king consort of Navarra. His changes in religious and political position influenced the first French wars of religion.
First King Bourbon of France and former King of Navarra. It ended much of the French religious wars and rebuilt the monarchical authority after decades of conflict.
King of France during the consolidation of the Bourbon monarchy. His reign was closely linked to Cardinal Richelieu's policy and to the French entry into the Thirty-Year War.
King of France for over seven decades and symbol of the absolute European monarchy. Versailles, the wars of expansion and dynastic politics defined their long reign.

The King of Spain whose government was dominated by the Duke of Lerma and an initially more peaceful foreign policy. His reign saw the expulsion of the Moorish and the beginning of the Thirty-Year War.

King of Spain during a stage of great cultural glow and strong political crises. His reign, associated with the condeduke of Olivares, was marked by European wars and the rebellions of Catalonia and Portugal.
He actively intervened in the crises of the French monarchy during the Hundred Years’ War. His naval and Norman domains allowed him to act on both sides of the Pyrenees.

King of Navarre during the second half of the twelfth century and the father of Sancho VII and Blanche of Navarre. His family connected the kingdom with Castile and Champagne. Blanche’s descendants were decisive in the succession of 1234, when the crown passed to Theobald I.
Consort of the Ivrea-Burgundy dynasty. Their career was connected to Navarre and Castile.
King of Navarre, famous for his participation at Las Navas de Tolosa. His long reign closed the direct male line of Navarre’s Jiménez dynasty.

Daughter of Sancho VI and sister of Sancho VII, she married Teobaldo III of Champagne. After widowing she held the position of her son Teobaldo during her minority. For her, that son gathered a Navarrese hereditary right that became effective when her uncle Sancho VII died.

Daughter of Sancho VI of Navarre, she married Ricardo I in Limassol (Cyprus) in 1191, during the crusade. She never lived in England; after widowing she lived in Le Mans, which was part of her dowry, and there she founded the Abbey of L’Épau, where she is buried.
The son of Louis XIV and heir of France, the Grand Dauphin. He died in 1711 before his father; his son Philip of Anjou was Philip V of Spain.
Prince of the House of Bourbon. Their life was connected with France, Navarre.
King of France for much of the 18th century. His reign combined courtesan prestige, costly wars and growing fiscal and political problems that would inherit the later monarchy.
Prince of the Bourbon dynasty. Their career was connected to France and Navarre.
Last King of France of the Old Regime. The financial crisis and the call for the General States led to the French Revolution, which ended with the monarchy and its implementation.
Last King Habsburg of Spain. His lack of offspring turned his succession into a European question and, after his death, he triggered the Spanish War of Succession.

First King of Spain. The War of Succession caused him to lose Milan, Naples and Sardinia; he recovered the latter briefly between 1717 and 1720. Its penisterial and Italian domains followed different paths.
The eldest son of Philip V, he reigned only a few months in 1724 after his father's abdication. He died of smallpox at the age of 17 and Philip V returned to the throne.
King of Spain between 1746 and 1759, son of Philip V and Mary Luisa of Savoy. He maintained a policy of neutrality and reforms with ministers such as Ensenada and Carvajal; he died without offspring.

He ruled Naples and Sicily since 1734 before inheriting the Spanish monarchy in 1759. Then he gave both Italian kingdoms to his son Fernando. His Spanish reign led to urban and administrative reforms.

King of Spain between 1788 and 1808, son of Charles III. His government, dominated by Godoy, lived the war with revolutionary France and Trafalgar; he abdicated in Aranjuez in favor of Fernando VII; Bayona's subsequent renunciation gave up his rights to Napoleon.
Known as Alain the Great, he inherited the lordship of Albret through the line of John of Tartas and Charles II. He married Françoise de Châtillon and sought to expand his house’s political position.

Wife of Alain de Albret, she was the mother of Juan III of Navarre and Carlota de Albret. Her offspring connect the French nobility heritages with the Navarren monarchy and the Borja. Her birth year is preserved as approximate, avoiding presenting a conventional figure as an exact date.

A daughter of Alain of Albret and Françoise de Châtillon, she was a sister of John III of Navarre. Her marriage to Cesare Borgia formed part of the political connections between the French monarchy and Italy.
personas.biografia: A daughter of Alain of Albret and Françoise de Châtillon, she was a sister of John III of Navarre. Her marriage to Cesare Borgia formed part of the political connections between the French monarchy and Italy. The relationship provides a direct path between the Navarrese royal family and the protagonists of papal politics.

personas.nombre: Joan of Navarre, Duchess of Brittany
personas.resumen: The daughter of Charles II of Navarra, first married John IV of Brittany and was the mother of several members of the next ducal generation. She later married Henry IV of England.

personas.nombre: Margaret of Foix, Duchess of Brittany
personas.resumen: A daughter of Gaston IV of Foix and Eleanor of Navarre, she married Francis II of Brittany and was the mother of Anne of Brittany. Her position provides a direct link between the Pyrenean houses and the Breton succession.

personas.nombre: Agnes of Navarre, Countess of Foix
personas.resumen: Daughter of Philip of Évreux and Juana II of Navarre, married Gaston Fébus. She was the mother of the Count's legitimate son, also called Gaston.

personas.nombre: John of Foix, Viscount of Narbonne
personas.resumen: The son of Gaston IV and Leonor of Navarre, he was the brother of Gaston, Prince of Viana, and uncle of Catherine of Navarre. He married Maria of Orleans. His sons Germana and Gaston of Nemours link this branch with the Aragonese court and with the French campaigns in Italy.

The daughter of Blanche I of Navarre and John of Aragon, and the sister of Charles of Viana and Eleanor. After Charles’s death she stood at the centre of the dispute over Navarrese succession rights against her father.

eventos.titulo: Marriage of Isabella of Castle and Fernando of Aragon
eventos.descripcion: The marriage union links the two main crowns of the Iberic peninsula without legalizing them into a single kingdom.
The capitulation of Granada before Elizabeth I and Ferdinand II puts an end to the naziri emirate, Muhammad XII, Boabdil, and his town.
Charles V demands Luther to retract. The reformer's refusal and the political protection of Frederick the Wise transform a theological dispute into a constitutional problem of the Empire.
The imperial forces defeat the French army and capture King Francis I.
Mooted imperial troops loot Rome during the Italian Wars.
The agreement legally accepts the coexistence of Catholic and Lutheran territories within the Empire and recognizes that religious unity can no longer be restored by mere imperial imposition.
Charles V gradually distributes his domains between the Spanish branch and the Austrian branch of the Habsburgés.
Philip II's naval expedition against England fails after fighting, logistical problems and adverse time.

eventos.titulo: Charles V is elected King of Romans
eventos.descripcion: The succession of Maximilian I makes the imperial choice a European competition. Carlos brings together the imperial crown with a dynastic heritage that extends from the Netherlands to Spain and America.
Philip Melanchthon presents to Charles V a systematic exhibition of the Lutheran faith, backed by several princes and cities of the Empire.
Charles V defeats the League of Esmalcalda and captures its two great leaders, but military victory does not succeed in restoring the religious unity of the Empire.

A few days after the wedding of Margaret of Valois and Henry of Navarra, Coligny's assassination attempt resulted in the killing of Hugonot leaders in Paris and a new wave of violence for the kingdom.
The death of Francis of Anjou makes Henry of Navarra an alleged heir. Enrique de Guisa reorganizes the Catholic League, backed from Spain, to prevent a Protestant from inheriting the French crown.
Henry III is assassinated after allying with Henry of Navarre against the League. His death ends the Valois-Angoulême line on the throne, and Henry of Navarre claims the crown as Henry IV.

The conversion of Henry IV removes one of the greatest challenges to his acceptance as a king. The League progressively lost its support and war was no longer a mere alternative between a Catholic and a Protestant king.

Henry IV promulgates the Edict of Nantes and grants Protestant civil rights and a limited framework of worship and security. The Bourbonic monarchy closed the great phase of the Wars of Religion without imposing complete confessional uniformity.

eventos.titulo: The inheritance of Alfonso once again secures
eventos.descripcion: At the death of Alfonso V, Aragon and Trinacria pass to his brother John II while Naples remains for his son Fernando. The personal union does not become a stable fusion of the crowns.

eventos.titulo: France and Aragon are distributed Naples
eventos.descripcion: Louis XII and Fernando the Catholic agree to share with themselves the kingdom of Federico I. The cooperation lasts for little: the challenges about the boundaries of partition turn old allies into enemies.

eventos.titulo: Cerignola: The Grand Captain changes the war
eventos.descripcion: The forces of Gonzalo Fernández de Córdoba defeat the French at Cerignola. The combined use of infantry, campaign fortification and firearms strengthens the Aragonese position in southern Italy.
A second great victory of the Grand Captain forces the French forces to withdraw. The balance that was born from the 1500 division was definitely broken in favor of Fernando.

eventos.titulo: Fernando gathers Naples and Trinacria under his crown
eventos.descripcion: The French defeat leaves Fernando the Catholic as King of Naples and Trinacria. The two parts of the old Sicilian monarchy share again sovereign, but will continue to be administered as different kingdoms.

eventos.titulo: Pius V gets the Holy League
eventos.descripcion: Pius V has an agreement between the Hispanic Monarchy, Venice and the Pontifical States. Philip II provides an essential part of the resources and his stepbrother Don Juan of Austria receives the supreme command of the Allied fleet.

name: Savoy
summary: Savoy grew as a collection of domains on both sides of the Alps. The title changed from comital to ducal in 1416, but its institutions and estates did not become uniform. Partitions among branches, minorities and marriages with Burgundy, Cyprus, France and the Habsburgs explain a history that goes beyond a list of dukes.

Noble of the Savoy dynasty. Their career was connected to France, Savoy.

A daughter of Henry IV of France and Marie de’ Medici, she married Victor Amadeus I of Savoy. After his death she defended her children’s government against princes of the ducal family, including Thomas Francis of Carignano.
people.biografia: A daughter of Henry IV of France and Marie de’ Medici, she married Victor Amadeus I of Savoy. After his death she defended her children’s government against princes of the ducal family, including Thomas Francis of Carignano. The dispute over the regency became entangled with French and Spanish intervention, turning a family conflict into an international war.

people.resumen: Duke of Savoy from 1630 to 1637 and husband of Christine of France, a daughter of Henry IV. Under the Treaty of Cherasco in 1631, he ceded Pinerolo to France.
Consort of the House of Savoy. Their life was connected with Bavaria, Savoy.
Duke of Savoy who took advantage of the Spanish War of Succession to raise the rank of his house. He first became king of Sicily and then king of Sardinia.

Brother of Amadeus IV, he received rights in Piedmont and ruled Flanders for his marriage to Joan. He was not the successor of his father in Savoy County.
Consort of the Fieschi dynasty. Their career was connected to Piedmont and Savoy.

Son of Thomas II, he entered the county after the death of his uncle Philip I. His position was consolidated by agreements with other branches of the family, which retained their own rights. Edward and Aimon succeeded in Savoy; by their marriages, the count also linked with Bâgé and Brabant.
Consort of the Bâgé dynasty. Their career was connected to Savoy.
Count of Savoy, 1323–1329. Count of the Savoy dynasty.

A younger son of Amadeus V, he inherited after his brother Edward, whose daughter also asserted succession rights. His marriage to Yolande of Montferrat linked the House of Savoy to the new Italian branch of the Palaiologoi.
people.biografia: A younger son of Amadeus V, he inherited after his brother Edward, whose daughter also asserted succession rights. His marriage to Yolande of Montferrat linked the House of Savoy to the new Italian branch of the Palaiologoi. He was the father of Amadeus VI and Blanche, through whom the family became connected with the Visconti of Milan.

people.resumen: A daughter of Theodore I of Montferrat, she married Aymon of Savoy. Her ancestry connected her to Emperor Andronikos II and to the Palaiologan heiress Yolanda, known as Irene in Byzantium.
people.biografia: A daughter of Theodore I of Montferrat, she married Aymon of Savoy. Her ancestry connected her to Emperor Andronikos II and to the Palaiologan heiress Yolanda, known as Irene in Byzantium. She was the mother of Amadeus VI and Blanche of Savoy; the marriage added a genealogical basis to later Savoyard claims to Montferrat.

people.resumen: Known as the Green Count, he belonged to the generation that strengthened Savoy’s political and military reach. He was the son of Aymon and Yolanda of Montferrat, bringing together Savoyard and Palaiologan ancestry.
Consort of the Bourbon dynasty. Their career was connected to Bourbon and Savoy.

The Red Count succeeded his father Amadeo VI and maintained the relationship with the French monarchy. He married Bona of Berry and was the father of Amadeo VIII. His early death left a child heir and opened a struggle for regency between the mother and the new count's grandmother.
Consort of the Valois dynasty. Their career was connected to France and Savoy.
He inherited as a child and became the first Duke of Savoy in 1416. The elevation in rank did not create a new dynasty.

The son of Amadeus VIII and Mary of Burgundy, he assumed government functions before becoming Duke. His marriage to Anna of Lusignan linked Savoy to Cyprus.

The daughter of King Janus of Cyprus, she married Louis of Savoy and brought a direct Lusignan connection to the Alpine court. Her many descendants established links with France, Milan and the Cypriot succession itself.

people.resumen: Duke of Savoy from 1465, in fragile health because of epilepsy. His wife Yolande of France exercised government in practice. He was beatified for his piety.
Consort of the House of Valois. Their life was connected with France, Savoy.
Duke of Savoy, 1472–1482. Duke of the Savoy dynasty.

He inherited the duchy from his brother Philibert I. His marriage to Blanche of Montferrat strengthened Savoy’s expectations of the Palaeologan inheritance, while intervention in Saluzzo brought him into conflict with French interests.

Son of Louis and Anne of Cyprus, he became duke after his brother Amadeus IX’s male descendants died out. His brief government preceded those of his sons Philibert II and Charles III, born from different marriages.
Consort of the House of Bourbon. Their life was connected with Bourbon, Savoy.
A consort of House Brosse whose life was connected with Savoy.
He inherited from his father Philip II and married Margaret of Austria. The marriage brought Savoy closer to the Habsburgs and the Low Countries.
Duke of Savoy between 1504 and 1553. In 1536 France occupied almost all of its states and Geneva consolidated its independence; their son Manuel Filiberto recovered them in 1559.
Consort of the Aviz dynasty. Their career was connected to Portugal and Savoy.

He inherited a duchy occupied largely by other powers. His service to Charles V and Philip II, and especially the victory of San Quintin, contributed to the territorial recovery agreed at Cateau-Cambresis.
A consort of House Valois-Angoulêmea whose life was connected with France, Savoy.
The son of Manuel Filiberto, he ruled in a scenario dominated by the rivalries between France and the Hispanic monarchy. His marriage to Catalina Micaela connected him to Philip II.

A daughter of Philip II and Elisabeth of Valois, she married Charles Emmanuel I of Savoy. Their marriage placed the duke’s descendants within both the Habsburg and Valois family networks. Their sons included Victor Amadeus I and Thomas Francis, through whom the Carignano branch continued.

A younger son of Charles Emmanuel I and Catherine Michelle of Spain, he founded the Savoy-Carignano branch. He married Marie de Bourbon, Countess of Soissons, and took part in the disputes over the regency of Christine of France.
Princess of Carignano of the House of Bourbon-Condé. Their life was connected with France, Savoy.

Son of Thomas Francis of Savoy-Carignano, he inherited from his mother the county of Soissons and served as a general in the armies of Louis XIV. He married Olympia Mancini, niece of Mazarino, and was the father of Prince Eugene.
Duke of Savoy, 1638–1675. Duke of the Savoy dynasty.
Consort of the Savoy-Nemours dynasty. Their career was connected to Savoy and France.
King of Sardinia and Duke of Savoy who continued the territorial expansion of his dynasty in northern Italy. It was actively involved in the great European wars of the 18th century.
Consort of the Hesse dynasty. Their life was connected with Hesse and Savoy.
King of Sardinia and Duke of Savoy since 1773. The war with revolutionary France cost him Savoy and Nice, given by the armistice of Cherasco in 1796.
Consort of the Bourbon dynasty. Their career was connected to Spain and Savoy.
King of Sardinia from 1796. French troops forced him to abandon his mainland territories in 1798; he took refuge in Sardinia and abdicated in favour of his brother Victor Emmanuel I in 1802.
Consort of the Bourbon dynasty. Their career was connected to France and Savoy.
He regained Piamonte and Saboya in 1814 and obtained Genoa at the Vienna Congress and Abdicted after the Piamontian liberal revolution in 1821.
King of Sardinia from 1821 to 1831, brother of Victor Emmanuel I. He restored absolutist government after the revolution of 1821 and was the last ruler of the main Savoy line.
A son of Thomas Francis and Marie of Bourbon-Soissons, he continued the Carignano branch. His marriage to Angela Caterina d’Este added an Italian connection to his Savoyard and Bourbon inheritance.
Princess of Carignano of the Este dynasty. Their life was connected with Modena and Savoy.

King of Sardinia since 1831, of the Savoy-Carignano branch. He granted the 1848 Statute and declared war on Austria; he won in Novara (1849), and abdicated in Victor Manuel II.

Daughter of Amadeus V of Savoy and wife of Andronikos III Paleologist. She was regent by her son John V during the civil war against Juan Cantacuceno (1341-1347).

eventos.descripcion: The marriage union links the two main crowns of the Iberic peninsula without legalizing them into a single kingdom.
The capitulation of Granada before Elizabeth I and Ferdinand II puts an end to the naziri emirate, Muhammad XII, Boabdil, and his town.
Charles V demands Luther to retract. The reformer's refusal and the political protection of Frederick the Wise transform a theological dispute into a constitutional problem of the Empire.
The imperial forces defeat the French army and capture King Francis I.
Mooted imperial troops loot Rome during the Italian Wars.
The agreement legally accepts the coexistence of Catholic and Lutheran territories within the Empire and recognizes that religious unity can no longer be restored by mere imperial imposition.
Charles V gradually distributes his domains between the Spanish branch and the Austrian branch of the Habsburgés.
Philip II's naval expedition against England fails after fighting, logistical problems and adverse time.

eventos.titulo: Charles V is elected King of Romans
eventos.descripcion: The succession of Maximilian I makes the imperial choice a European competition. Carlos brings together the imperial crown with a dynastic heritage that extends from the Netherlands to Spain and America.
Philip Melanchthon presents to Charles V a systematic exhibition of the Lutheran faith, backed by several princes and cities of the Empire.
Charles V defeats the League of Esmalcalda and captures its two great leaders, but military victory does not succeed in restoring the religious unity of the Empire.
The death of Francis of Anjou makes Henry of Navarra an alleged heir. Enrique de Guisa reorganizes the Catholic League, backed from Spain, to prevent a Protestant from inheriting the French crown.
After years of war, the Sicians hold up Federico, son of Peter III and Constance of Hohenstaufen. The island develops its own political line opposite the Andean Naples.

Alfonso V. of Aragon defeats the angevine resistance and enters Naples. For the first time since the Visperas, an same monarch controls Aragon, Trinacria and the mainland kingdom, though the crowns have separate identities.

eventos.titulo: The inheritance of Alfonso once again secures
eventos.descripcion: At the death of Alfonso V, Aragon and Trinacria pass to his brother John II while Naples remains for his son Fernando. The personal union does not become a stable fusion of the crowns.

eventos.titulo: France and Aragon are distributed Naples
eventos.descripcion: Louis XII and Fernando the Catholic agree to share with themselves the kingdom of Federico I. The cooperation lasts for little: the challenges about the boundaries of partition turn old allies into enemies.

eventos.titulo: Cerignola: The Grand Captain changes the war
eventos.descripcion: The forces of Gonzalo Fernández de Córdoba defeat the French at Cerignola. The combined use of infantry, campaign fortification and firearms strengthens the Aragonese position in southern Italy.
A second great victory of the Grand Captain forces the French forces to withdraw. The balance that was born from the 1500 division was definitely broken in favor of Fernando.

eventos.titulo: Fernando gathers Naples and Trinacria under his crown
eventos.descripcion: The French defeat leaves Fernando the Catholic as King of Naples and Trinacria. The two parts of the old Sicilian monarchy share again sovereign, but will continue to be administered as different kingdoms.

eventos.titulo: Pius V gets the Holy League
eventos.descripcion: Pius V has an agreement between the Hispanic Monarchy, Venice and the Pontifical States. Philip II provides an essential part of the resources and his stepbrother Don Juan of Austria receives the supreme command of the Allied fleet.

eventos.titulo: The king's resignation does not force the island
eventos.descripcion: Jaime II agreed to leave his claim to Sicily at Anagni, but the Sicilians did not accept to come back to Angevin rule. They chose his brother Federico and forced the House of Barcelona to divide about his future.

Mary and Martin came to Sicily with Aragonese support to put their arms at the Barons. The Queen's hereditary legitimacy was insufficient without his military capacity. The island's government again closely linked with the Aragon's Crown.

name: Burgundy
summary: The Duchy of Burgundy, incorporated into the French Crown after the death of Charles the Bold in 1477, was not the same territory as the imperial County of Burgundy, or Franche-Comté. Mary of Burgundy’s inheritance also included lands in the Netherlands. The Habsburgs retained the ducal title, but that title does not justify showing the duchy as an effective domain of Philip I or Charles V.
notes: Duchy incorporated into the French Crown after 1477; it is not equivalent to the imperial County of Burgundy or to all the lands of the Valois dukes. The Habsburgs’ later ducal dignity is recorded as titular.

eventos.titulo: Marriage of Philip and Margaret of Flanders

The imperial forces defeat the French army and capture King Francis I.
Mooted imperial troops loot Rome during the Italian Wars.

Philip II's naval expedition against England fails after fighting, logistical problems and adverse time.
The Worms Diet promotes common mechanisms of justice, public peace and political organization that seek to make a rule of an Empire with hundreds of territorial powers.

John II's extramatrimonial son, obtained Mamluk help to fight the crown to Carlota and recovered Famagusta from the genoese. His marriage to Catherine Cornaro reinforced the Venetian influence. He died before the birth of his heir.

Born after James II’s death, he inherited the crown under Catherine Cornaro’s regency. His death in infancy left his mother as queen and facilitated the extension of Venetian guardianship over Cyprus.

eventos.descripcion: After the collapse of the Hohenstaufen authority, several rival kings are fighting an imperial crown whose ability to impose obedience is deeply weakened.
Frederick II’s death leaves his Kingdom of Sicily in the hands of a Hohenstaufen dynasty at odds with the papacy. Conrad IV inherits the crown while Manfred maintains the family’s position in Italy.
Conradino invades Italy to recover his family's inheritance, but is defeated in Tagliacozzo and executed in Naples. Carlos de Anjou is left as the owner of the old Hohenstaufen kingdom.
The young Balduino IV gets an unexpected victory about Saladino near Montgisard.
Saladin destroys the main army of the Kingdom of Jerusalem at Hattin, leaving the capital practically defenseless.
The Belian of Ibelin negotiates Jerusalem's surrender to Saladin after organizing his defense of the city.

eventos.titulo: Federico II recovers Jerusalem by treaty
eventos.descripcion: The Sixth Crusade temporarily returns Jerusalem to frank control through negotiation, strengthening the link of the Jerosobimitana crown with the Hohenstaufen.
The fall of Acre removes the last great territorial centre of the Kingdom of Jerusalem in the Holy Land and the crown has been surviving as a dynastic title attached to Cyprus.
Juana had chosen Louis of Anjou as heir, but Carlos of Durazzo conquered the kingdom. His death and that of Juana left the next generation a war between Anjou and Durazzo, not a peaceful succession.

eventos.descripcion: The Varna crusade ends with an Ottoman victory and the death of King Vladimir III.
Mehmed II conquers Constantinople; Constantine XI dies in its defence and the Byzantine Empire comes to an end.

The fleet of the Holy League, led by Don Juan of Austria and composed mainly of forces of the Hispanic Monarchy, Venice and the Pontifical States, defeats the Ottoman army of Ali Bajá after hours of combat of galera against galera. The Ottoman center is falling apart, Uluç Ali is able to save part of its wing and thousands of combatants are killed, injured or held captive. The victory does not drive the Ottoman Empire out of the Mediterranean, but it destroys much of its combat fleet and becomes a huge political and symbolic victory of the coalition.

eventos.titulo: The battle and help of Vienna
eventos.descripcion: The relief army led by John III Sobieski, with Polish, Habsburg and Holy Roman Empire forces, breaks the Ottoman siege of Vienna on 12 September 1683. The victory opens a new phase of the war in Hungary and strengthens the rise of the Habsburg monarchy in central Europe.

eventos.titulo: Soliman and the great Ottoman advance
eventos.descripcion: The long reign of Soliman I takes Ottoman power to one of its greatest expansions. The Eastern Mediterranean and Central Europe have become a permanent front for competition with the Christian powers.

eventos.titulo: Selim II inherits the Ottoman Empire
eventos.descripcion: The death of Soliman leads to Selim II. The new reign keeps the pressure on the Venetian and Spanish domains of the Mediterranean.

eventos.titulo: The invasion of Cyprus forces Venice to seek allies
eventos.descripcion: The Ottoman offensive against Cyprus challenges one of the great Venetian possessions of the Levant. Venice needs to turn its particular war into a more extensive coalition.

The League has Barbarigo on the left wing, Don Juan and Colonna in the center, Gianandrea Doria on the right and Álvaro de Bazán in front of the reserve. In front of them, Ali Bajá runs the Ottoman center and Uluç Ali sends the wing facing Doria.

In the center, the Royal Galera of Don Juan and the Sultana of Ali Bajá are stuck in a struggle of approaches, archauces and successive reinforcements. The fall of Ali Bajá and the take of his ship disorganize the Ottoman center and make the central combat the symbolic core of victory.

eventos.titulo: The wings have nearly changed the result.
eventos.descripcion: Barbarigo is morally injured in the Christian left wing. At the opposite end, Uluç Ali takes advantage of the open space during Doria's maneuver and hits several League galleys. The reservation of Alvaro de Bazan comes to close the gap, while Uluç Ali manages to withdraw with part of his ships.

eventos.titulo: Uluç Ali Rebuilds the Ottoman Armed
eventos.descripcion: Uluç Ali, one of the few great Ottoman commanders that manages to save his squadron at Lepanto, is elevated to naval command. The imperial arsenals quickly rebuild a fleet capable of returning to the Mediterranean the following year.

eventos.titulo: The victory does not return Cyprus
eventos.descripcion: Venice signs peace with the Ottoman Empire and renounces Cyprus. Lepanto has been an extraordinary naval victory but not an Ottoman expulsion from the Mediterranean: strategic balance continues.

eventos.titulo: The Hungarian Rebellion Openes a Door to the Sultan
eventos.descripcion: Imre Thököly leads Hungarian opposition to the Habsburgs and seeks Ottoman support. The internal conflict within Leopold I’s monarchy becomes entangled with imperial rivalry in central Europe.

The great visir Kara Mustafa leads the Ottoman army to Vienna. Leopold leaves the capital and Ernst Rüdiger von Starhemberg organizes the defense while fortifications suffer weeks of siege and mine work.
The conquest of Buda shows that Vienna was not an isolated episode. The war begun in 1683 develops into Habsburg expansion across Hungary and permanently alters the balance of central Europe.
The campaign of 1462 pitted Vlad III against Mehmed II and opened a new struggle for the Wallachian throne, in which Radu the Fair received Ottoman support.
The forces of Mehmed II conquer the kingdom of Bosnia; the last king, Stephen Tomašević, is captured and executed.

The Branković ruled from Smederevo, experienced an Ottoman interruption and eventually retained titles in Hungarian exile. Marriages with the Kotromanić and Rareș families trace the continuity of their descendants after the state was lost.

Son of Stephen Thomas and Vojača, he married Jelena, daughter of the Serbian despot Lazar Branković. The link accompanied its short Serbian access of 1459, before the fall of Smedereo.

Wife of Stephen I Kotroman and mother of Esteban II and Vladislav, is part of the Serbian descent invoked by the Kotromanić. Her grandchildren Isabel of Bosnia and Tvrtko I allow to follow different connections: the Hungarian monarchy and the construction of Bosnian royalty.

Wife of Stefan Branković, shared the family's displacement after the loss of Serbian power. Her sons Đorđe and Jovan preserved the dignity of despots in the Hungarian sphere. Her religious memory was linked to Krušedol and the preservation of the dynastic tradition in exile.

The son of Stefan and Angelina, he retained the title of Serbian despot in exile. He left the secular life and took the name of Maximus. His religious activity and his relationship with Krušedol continued the presence of the family in the region. It should not be confused with the 17th century homonymous historian.

The son of Stefan and Angelina, he initially shared the dignity of despot with his brother Đorđe. The title was held in the Hungarian political sphere and did not entail the recovery of Serbia. His daughter Elena married Petru Rareș, so the descendants of the Branković linked with the Moldovan court.

A daughter of Jovan Branković and wife of Petru Rareș, she brought a connection with the Serbian despots to Moldavia. She took part in government during her son Stephen’s minority. Her daughter Ruxandra also became a Moldavian consort and regent; Chiajna, Petru’s daughter by another union, was her stepdaughter.

name: Foix
summary: The County of Foix connected the noble networks of southern France with lands beyond the Pyrenees. Roger Bernard III’s marriage to Margaret of Béarn united inheritances with distinct titles and institutions. The death of Gaston Fébus’s son diverted the succession to the Castellbò branch. Matthew and then Isabella inherited the whole; descendants of Isabella’s marriage to Archambaud of Grailly continued to use the Foix name. The marriage of Gaston IV and Eleanor of Navarre opened the path to a crown inherited by their grandchildren Francis Phoebus and Catherine. The descendants of Catherine and John of Albret continued that family line under another house.

eventos.descripcion: A few days after the wedding of Margaret of Valois and Henry of Navarra, Coligny's assassination attempt resulted in the killing of Hugonot leaders in Paris and a new wave of violence for the kingdom.
The death of Francis of Anjou makes Henry of Navarra an alleged heir. Enrique de Guisa reorganizes the Catholic League, backed from Spain, to prevent a Protestant from inheriting the French crown.
Henry III is assassinated after allying with Henry of Navarre against the League. His death ends the Valois-Angoulême line on the throne, and Henry of Navarre claims the crown as Henry IV.

The conversion of Henry IV removes one of the greatest challenges to his acceptance as a king. The League progressively lost its support and war was no longer a mere alternative between a Catholic and a Protestant king.

Henry IV promulgates the Edict of Nantes and grants Protestant civil rights and a limited framework of worship and security. The Bourbonic monarchy closed the great phase of the Wars of Religion without imposing complete confessional uniformity.

name: Kartli-Kakheti
summary: Heraclius II united the two eastern monarchies in 1762. The union did not incorporate Imereti or remove Persian and Russian pressure. The Treaty of Georgievsk did not prevent the invasion of 1795; the brief reign of George XII preceded annexation by Russia.
notes: The union of the two eastern kingdoms since 1762 and does not include Imereti and does not have an equivalent to all of Georgia.

people.resumen: It promoted Georgian legal codification, printing and written culture. His career was conditioned by Persian investiture, Ottoman pressure and Russian aid that failed to consolidate his power; he ended up exiled in Russia.
A daughter of Vakhtang VI and wife of Teimuraz II, she linked the branches of Kartli and Kakheti. She was the mother of Heraclius II, who united both crowns in 1762.

His collaboration with Nader Shah favored the recognition of his power in Kartli. He and his son Heraclio ruled neighbouring crowns and sought external support to support their position after the collapse of the Nader empire.

He gathered Kartli and Kakheti in 1762 and tried to strengthen the eastern kingdom. The Gueorguievsk treaty linked him to Russia, but did not prevent Aga Mohamed Khan's attack on Tbilis in 1795. His career connects Georgian politics with Persia and Russian expansion.

The Western rebellion and its capture by the atabeg of Samtskhe broke its authority. After losing control of Kartli, he established his own monarchy in Kakheti. It is the same person known there as George I, origin of the later Kakheti royal branch.

He disputed the legacy of the united monarchy, but eventually recognized the separation of Kakheti and Imereti. His kingdom was centered in Kartli. His children continued to the royal line and the main branch of Mukhrani.

The rivalry with Kakheti and the safapivid expansion conditioned his reign. He temporarily incorporated the neighbouring kingdom, which later regained its autonomy. His abdication left the crown first to his brother and then to his son Luarsab.

Brother of David X, he assumed the crown after his abdication and gave it to his nephew Luarsab. His brief government links two generations of the Bagrationi in a period of increasing Persian intervention.

personas.resumen: The son of Mary of Burgundy and Maximilian of Habsburg, he inherited the Netherlands and, after Senlis (1493), the County of Burgundy and Artois. He preserved the dignity of the Duke of Burgundy, although the duchy was under the French Crown. His marriage to Juana I took him to Castile and transmitted different assets to Charles V.

Emperor of the Holy Empire and sovereign of a composite monarchy that reached the Iberian peninsula, Italy, the Netherlands and America. From Philip I he inherited the County of Burgundy, Artois, Namur and Luxembourg, as well as other Dutch territories. He then incorporated Frisia, Utrecht, Overijssel, Drente, Groninga and Güeldres in a step-by-step manner between 1524 and 1543. He preserved the ducal dignity of Burgundy, but did not rule the duchy incorporated into France. Since 1535, Milan has been under imperial control; Philip II's invasion and subsequent possession must be distinguished from that government.

eventos.descripcion: The election of Francisco Esteban returns the crown to the dynastic environment of Mary Teresa and creates the Habsburgo-Lorraine line.
Joseph II succeeded his father as emperor and, after 1780, tried to reform the Habsburg domains quickly, repeatedly colliding with territorial and corporate privileges.
The revolution in France alters the European political balance and makes the fate of Mary Antonieta, sister of Joseph II and Leopold II, an international dynastic problem.
Francis II inherits the imperial crown in the midst of revolutionary war. As 1800 arrived, the old Empire still existed, but it was facing a transformation that would end a few years later.

name: Albret
summary: The Lordship of Albret gave its name to a south-western French house that grew through alliances, court service and the accumulation of estates. Charles I, Constable of France, died at Agincourt; his descendants carried the inheritance to Alain the Great. John of Albret’s marriage to Catherine of Navarre added a royal connection without turning the French lordship and the Pyrenean kingdom into a single entity. Albret’s elevation to a duchy in 1550 belongs to a later period. The profiles distinguish lordly or ducal title from the holders’ Navarrese rights.
notes: A lordship of the House of Albret, raised to a duchy in the sixteenth century; distinct from the Kingdom of Navarre.

people.resumen: He maintained the Albret's claim on the Peninsular Navarre after the conquest. His marriage to Marguerite of Navarre turned his court into a focus of Renaissance culture.
He adopted the Reformation and turned his domains into a fundamental support of the Hugonote cause. He was the mother of Henry of Navarra, future Henry IV of France.
First King Bourbon of France and former King of Navarra. It ended much of the French religious wars and rebuilt the monarchical authority after decades of conflict.
Known as Alain the Great, he inherited the lordship of Albret through the line of John of Tartas and Charles II. He married Françoise de Châtillon and sought to expand his house’s political position.

The son of Arnaud- Amanieu of Albret and Margarita of Bourbon, was lord of Albret and constable of France. He died in the battle of Azinchurt in 1415. His offspring connected the house both with the Foix, for his daughter Juana, and with the line that led to Alain and the Navarre kings of Albret.

people.nombre: Joan of Albret, Countess of Foix
people.resumen: The daughter of Charles I of Albret, she married John I of Foix and was the mother of Gaston IV. This marriage connected the Albret with the Foix-Grailly line before the later link of Catherine of Navarre and John III of Albret. Her presence reveals a family connection prior to the most well-known royal union.
Lord of Albret in the 14th century, he married Margaret of Bourbon. Her offspring combined the French southwest heritage with ties close to the royal family.

people.nombre: Margaret of Bourbon, Lady of Albret
people.resumen: A daughter of Peter I of Bourbon and Isabella of Valois, she married Arnaud Amanieu of Albret and was the mother of Charles I. Her descent connected the Albrets with two Capetian lines and shows how marriage could add court relationships to a house’s territorial inheritance.

people.nombre: John of Albret, Viscount of Tartas
people.resumen: A son of Charles II of Albret and father of Alain, he died before his own father. translatedSource.nota: A lordship of the House of Albret, raised to a duchy in the sixteenth century; distinct from the Kingdom of Navarre.
translatedSource.resumen: The Lordship of Albret gave its name to a south-western French house that grew through alliances, court service and the accumulation of estates. Charles I, Constable of France, died at Agincourt; his descendants carried the inheritance to Alain the Great. John of Albret’s marriage to Catherine of Navarre added a royal connection without turning the French lordship and the Pyrenean kingdom into a single entity. Albret’s elevation to a duchy in 1550 belongs to a later period. The profiles distinguish lordly or ducal title from the holders’ Navarrese rights.

eventos.descripcion: A few days after the wedding of Margaret of Valois and Henry of Navarra, Coligny's assassination attempt resulted in the killing of Hugonot leaders in Paris and a new wave of violence for the kingdom.
The death of Francis of Anjou makes Henry of Navarra an alleged heir. Enrique de Guisa reorganizes the Catholic League, backed from Spain, to prevent a Protestant from inheriting the French crown.
Henry III is assassinated after allying with Henry of Navarre against the League. His death ends the Valois-Angoulême line on the throne, and Henry of Navarre claims the crown as Henry IV.

The conversion of Henry IV removes one of the greatest challenges to his acceptance as a king. The League progressively lost its support and war was no longer a mere alternative between a Catholic and a Protestant king.

Henry IV promulgates the Edict of Nantes and grants Protestant civil rights and a limited framework of worship and security. The Bourbonic monarchy closed the great phase of the Wars of Religion without imposing complete confessional uniformity.

name: Tripoli
summary: The Latin County of Tripoli passed from the house of Toulouse to the house of Poitiers. It shared rulers with Antioch without losing its identity and survived that principality’s fall. Tensions among counts, the commune, Genoa and local families preceded the Mamluk conquest.

people.resumen: Count of Tripoli and one of the great barons of the kingdom. He acted as regent and was a central figure in the political struggles that preceded Hattin.

He brought together the County of Tripoli and Principality of Antioch, although he temporarily lost the latter to Raymond-Roupen. The union was personal, with each territory retaining its title and interests. His son Henry connects this house with the kings of Cyprus.

He maintained the dynastic union of Antioch and Tripoli. His marriage to Lucienne of Segni linked the House of Poitiers to the Italian aristocracy, and their son Bohemond VI inherited both states during a transformation of the Latin East.

He married Sibylla of Armenia and joined the Christian powers’ rapprochement with the Mongols. The Mamluk conquest of Antioch in 1268 left him ruling Tripoli and retaining the title to the lost principality.

Daughter of Hetum I and wife of Bohemundo VI. Her marriage reinforced the alliance between Armenia, Antioch and Tripoli; after the death of her husband she intervened in county politics during the Bohemundo VII minority.

He governed Tripoli during the county’s final years and retained the title of Antioch after the city’s loss. Conflicts with the Embriacos and Templars weakened the state before the Mamluk attack of 1289.
A sister and heiress of Bohemond VII, she returned from Italy to claim Tripoli. She had to negotiate with the commune and with Genoa before Qalawun’s conquest in 1289 ended the Latin county.

Reformist princes and cities protest against the reversal of religious concessions. The name that will end up identifying the Protestant churches is born from this political protest.

Charles V defeats the League of Esmalcalda and captures its two great leaders, but military victory does not succeed in restoring the religious unity of the Empire.

people.resumen: Viscount of Béziers and, from 1150, of Carcassonne and Razès. In 1157 he acknowledged the overlordship of Raymond Berengar IV of Barcelona over his viscounties. He was killed in 1167 by the townspeople of Béziers, incited by the Count of Toulouse.

Son of Raymond Trencavel I, Viscount of Carcassonne, Béziers, Albi and Razès since 1167. That year he recognized the sovereignty of Alfonso II of Aragon. He married Adelaide of Toulouse and protected the Cathars in their lands.

A son of Roger II, he was Viscount of Carcassonne, Razès, Béziers and Albi from 1194. In 1209 the Albigensian Crusade sacked Béziers and besieged Carcassonne. He was seized during negotiations and died in prison that year, perhaps poisoned; his lands passed to Simon de Montfort.

Son of Raymond Roger, took refuge with the Count of Foix and then in the court of James I. He briefly recovered Carcassonne between 1224 and 1227 and tried again in 1240; in 1247 he gave his dominions to the king of France in exchange for a pension.

name: Desmond
summary: The Gaelic kingdom of the MacCarthys survived Anglo-Norman expansion as a network of powers and lordships. The MacCarthy Mór held authority distinct from the FitzGerald Earldom of Desmond. Relations with the Tudors transformed titles and forms of succession.
notes: Kingdom and later Gaelic lordship of the MacCarthys. It was distinct from the FitzGerald earldom, although both powers operated in southern Ireland.

people.resumen: He ruled the Gaelic Kingdom of Desmond during the Anglonormands expansion in southern Ireland. The continuation of the MacCarthy after his death allows us to distinguish this royalty from the County of Desmond that later will be received by the Fitzgerald.

Head of the MacCarthy Mór, accepted the title of Count of Clancare within the Tudor policy. His daughter Ellen inherited a central position in the dispute over family domains. Gaelic royalty, the head of the city and the county are not presented as equivalent charges.

Daughter and heiress of Donal MacCarthy Mor, her marriage to Florence MacCarthy united rival claims over family domains. Her heritage placed her at the center of the struggle between the Gaelic branches and the Crown administration.

His marriage with Ellen became a central figure of the MacCarthy Mór's succession. He negotiated with the Crown and with the Gaelic leaders during the 9-year war. He spent most of his later life incarcerated in England.
